source.title: Clipped Hyperbolic Classifiers Are Super-Hyperbolic Classifiers
source.authors: Yunhui Guo; Xu-Dong Wang; Yu-Bei Chen; Stella X. Yu

record.file_problem: Full paper text, including supplementary sections, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper studies vanishing gradients in hyperbolic neural networks, but does not measure the training classification error or test any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test accuracy comparisons and a training-loss/gradient observation. The test-accuracy results do not measure training classification error; the training-loss observation is recorded under fits_no_version. No other results meet the row criteria.
record.test_reason: The study measures vanishing gradients in hybrid Euclidean–hyperbolic classifiers and evaluates feature clipping. It does not measure CIFAR training classification error, compare initialization or trainable depth, or test the width, shortcut, learning-rate stability, or batch-normalization effects specified in V1–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors attribute baseline HNNs' poorer general classification performance to vanishing gradients in the hybrid architecture and propose Euclidean feature clipping as a remedy. They report improved benchmark accuracy, few-shot performance, adversarial robustness, and out-of-distribution detection.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains hybrid Euclidean-hyperbolic classifiers and adds Euclidean feature clipping; it does not use the recipes or measure the training classification-error outcomes in the listed versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The supplementary discussion reports that clipping radius affects test accuracy: too large a radius is associated with vanishing gradients, while too small a radius reduces capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: In the MNIST hybrid classifier, embeddings approach the Poincaré-ball boundary; late in training, gradients vanish while training loss slightly increases.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Hybrid Euclidean–hyperbolic classifiers can develop vanishing gradients as hyperbolic embeddings approach the Poincaré-ball boundary, impeding optimization of their Euclidean parameters.

record.problems: The training-loss/gradient result is described qualitatively and illustrated in a figure; no numerical training-classification-error result is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Standard benchmark classification results and few-shot, adversarial robustness, and OOD results concern test performance or other measures, not the training classification error named in the claim versions.

untested.parts: Near-zero CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 training classification error, including corrupted labels, and dependence on model size, stopping, or regularization.
Spurious local minima and extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training degradation with depth, prevention by identity shortcuts, and the specified initialization and normalization exceptions.
Effects of activation-matched initialization, orthogonal versus Gaussian weights, and convolutional initialization on training speed and trainable depth.
Recovery above initial stability limits, curvature reduction, edge-of-stability dynamics, and divergence below the initial threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and tolerated learning rates, and comparable training without normalization using Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: References to initialization, residual architectures, and dynamical isometry provide background or model choices rather than tests of the listed versions. The omitted test-performance comparisons do not supply the missing training-error or controlled intervention evidence.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, corrupted or random labels, model size, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious minima, and student width.
Depth, identity shortcuts, plain networks, special initialization, and normalization removal.
Learning-rate stability, curvature, and sharpness behavior.
Batch normalization comparisons and Fixup training.

rows.subject: LeNet-like convolutional neural network with hyperbolic classifier
rows.size_stated: two convolutional layers with max pooling layers in between and three fully connected layers
rows.operation_detail: Tracked hyperbolic embedding trajectories, gradient magnitude, and training loss during training on MNIST.
rows.measure: Training loss and gradient magnitude during training
rows.value: At the end of training, the training loss slightly increases while the gradient vanishes.
rows.note: The reported loss and gradient behavior does not establish training classification error.
rows.check: The qualitative loss increase and vanishing gradient are accurately reported in Section 3.2 and Figure 4, but establish none of V1–V6. In particular, training loss does not establish training classification error, and this experiment does not compare initializations.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
